name: Old Norse
blurb: Old Norse was carved in runes, the Younger Futhark of sixteen letters, on stones, wood and bone; from the 11th and 12th centuries it was also written in the Latin alphabet.

scripts.label: Long-branch runes
scripts.about: The long-branch runes (“Danish” runes) of the Viking Age, carved on the great stones of Denmark such as Harald Bluetooth’s at Jelling, around 965.
scripts.note: Type Old Norse or any name: the sixteen runes stand for more sounds than they have letters, so d is written as t, g as k, e as i, and o, v, w and y as u, as the carvers did. A doubled letter is written once. ʀ (on its key) is the r that came from an older z. Spaces become the small dot between words.
groups: úr · u, o, v, w, y
óss · a nasal a, later o
ýr · an r at the end of a word (from an older z)
samples: haraltr kunukʀ baþ kaurua kubl þausi aft kurm faþur sin
“King Harald ordered these monuments made in memory of Gorm, his father”: the larger Jelling stone, about 965
“Thor, hallow these runes!”: the Glavendrup stone on Funen

scripts.label: Short-twig runes
scripts.about: The short-twig runes (“Swedish-Norwegian” runes), quicker to cut, used in Sweden and Norway from the 9th century, as on the Rök stone.
scripts.note: The same sixteen runes in their shorter forms. Type as for the long-branch runes: d is written as t, g as k, e as i, o, v, w and y as u; a doubled letter is written once.
